Jetzt ermittelt die Polizei. Von Christina Strunk, Jannis Weiser Seit Sonntagabend gegen 22 Uhr ist die Strecke zwischen Marl-Sinsen und Marl-Lippe im Kreis Recklinghausen wieder freigegeben. Das hat ein Sprecher der Deutschen Bahn bestätigt. Beschädigte Kabel hatten dort für massive Probleme im Regionalverkehr gesorgt. Besonders betroffen war die Region Dülmen im Kreis Coesfeld . Auf der Strecke des RE42 endeten die Züge aus Richtung Münster in Haltern am See. Die Folge waren Teilausfälle zwischen Haltern am See und Recklinghausen Hauptbahnhof. S-Bahnen zwischen Wuppertal-Vohwinkel und Recklinghausen endeten und begannen in Essen Hbf . Außerdem kann es zu Teilausfällen zwischen Essen und Recklinghausen. Ein Ersatzverkehr wurde eingerichtet. Bundespolizei und Staatsschutz ermitteln nach Kabelklau Wie ein Sprecher der Bundespolizei in Dortmund am Montagmorgen erklärte, ermitteln die Beamten jetzt wegen Diebstahls. Denn die Kabel seien gezielt durchgeschnitten und entwendet worden. Weil die Ermittlungen noch nicht abgeschlossen sind, ist auch der Staatsschutz noch in den Fall involviert. Dies sei aber nur eine reine Routinemaßnahme, solange nicht ausgeschlossen werden könne, dass es sich um einen gezielten Sabotageakt handelt, so der Sprecher der Bundespolizei. title: Vorschau: Bezzel & Schwarz - Die Grenzgänger • Auf Schloss Neuschwanstein
description: 3sat am 05.09.2026: Sebastian Bezzel und Simon Schwarz schauen hinter die Kulissen von Schloss Neuschwanstein und Schloss Hohenschwangau. Sie treffen auf Luitpold Prinz von Bayern, einen Nachfahren von Ludwig III., und kreieren ihr eigenes Ludwig-Kunstwerk. In der Folge 'Schloss Neuschwanstein' schauen Simon Schwarz und Sebastian Bezzel hinter die Kulissen eines der berühmtesten Bauwerke der Welt. Nachdem sie von der Kutscherin Luise Pfeiffer zum großen Eingangsportal von Schloss Neuschwanstein gefahren wurden, führt Kastellanin Martina Neuner die beiden durch die beeindruckenden Säle und Gänge. Techniker Jürgen Hencir nimmt sie mit in die für die Öffentlichkeit verborgenen Ecken des riesigen Schlosses. Simon Schwarz und Sebastian Bezzel treffen zudem den heutigen Schlossherren Christian Luksch. Doch die Gemeinde Schwangau hat noch einen weiteren Touristenmagneten zu bieten: Schloss Hohenschwangau. Dort treffen sie Luitpold Prinz von Bayern, den Urenkel von Ludwig III. Beim Gang durch das Schloss erzählt er den Grenzgängern von seiner Familiengeschichte. Mit dem Künstler Robert Wilhelm kreieren Simon Schwarz und Sebastian Bezzel ihr ganz eigenes Bild von Ludwig II. - aber nicht mit dem Pinsel, sondern mit der Spraydose. Und mit der Touristenführerin Erih Gößler wandeln die beiden am Ufer des Alpsees auf den Spuren der Königsfamilie. Natürlich darf in Hohenschwangau der Besuch eines Souvenirladens nicht fehlen. Dort erklärt ihnen Barbara Stöger, was die größten Renner bei den mehr als einer Million Touristen sind, die jedes Jahr nach Hohenschwangau kommen.

Techniker Jürgen Hencir nimmt sie mit in die für die Öffentlichkeit verborgenen Ecken des riesigen Schlosses. Simon Schwarz und Sebastian Bezzel treffen zudem den heutigen Schlossherren Christian Luksch. Doch die Gemeinde Schwangau hat noch einen weiteren Touristenmagneten zu bieten: Schloss Hohenschwangau. Dort treffen sie Luitpold Prinz von Bayern, den Urenkel von Ludwig III. Beim Gang durch das Schloss erzählt er den Grenzgängern von seiner Familiengeschichte. Mit dem Künstler Robert Wilhelm kreieren Simon Schwarz und Sebastian Bezzel ihr ganz eigenes Bild von Ludwig II. - aber nicht mit dem Pinsel, sondern mit der Spraydose. Und mit der Touristenführerin Erih Gößler wandeln die beiden am Ufer des Alpsees auf den Spuren der Königsfamilie. Natürlich darf in Hohenschwangau der Besuch eines Souvenirladens nicht fehlen. Dort erklärt ihnen Barbara Stöger, was die größten Renner bei den mehr als einer Million Touristen sind, die jedes Jahr nach Hohenschwangau kommen. You have an idea for a video. You know what you want it to look like. But the moment you open a video editing app, you freeze. Where do you even start? I’m Shelly Puri, Product Marketing Manager on the Instagram and Edits teams. I get to spend my time talking with creators at every stage of their journey, from people posting their very first reel to creators who’ve been creating content for years. And one thing I hear over and over again is that getting started can be the hardest part. So I wanted to write this for anyone who’s been sitting on that first idea. Your first video edit doesn’t need to be perfect. It just needs to exist. And with Edits , Instagram’s free video creation app made with creators, for creators, you can capture content, edit an elevated social-first cut and get personalized insights to inspire your next video. It’s a creative studio that supports you from first idea to final edit, all in one place. You can go from “I have a clip” to “I have a Reel” in about five minutes! Let’s walk through it together. Open Edits and pick a clip. Tap the plus icon to start a new project. You’ll see your camera roll. Pick one clip. Just one. It can be anything: your coffee this morning, your dog doing something ridiculous, a sunset you filmed last week. Tap it, and it drops onto the timeline. That’s it. You already have a video. Technically, you could post it right now. But let’s make it a little more fun. Add some text. Tap the text tool and type something simple. A description, a joke, a question. Drag it wherever you want it onscreen. The safe zones will show you where it won’t get cut off by Instagram’s interface, so your text always lands exactly where you intend it. Now tap the animation menu and choose a style. Fade in. Bounce. Typewriter. Pick whatever feels right. There’s no wrong answer here. Drop in some music. Tap the audio icon and you’ll see Instagram’s full music library right inside the app. Search for a royalty-free song to use in a brand video or, browse audio that’s trending. Tap once to preview, tap again to add it to your timeline. Edits will trim the track to match your clip length automatically, so you don’t have to worry about cutting audio manually. If you want to get more precise later, you can adjust exactly which part of the song plays. But for now, let the app do the work. Watch it back. Scrub through the timeline with your finger. Watch your clip play with the text animation and the music together. This is your reel, you made it, and it probably took about three minutes! Post it (or save it for later). Tap the export button in the top right. Edits will process your video and give you the option to post directly to Instagram or download it to post anywhere you’d like. If you’re not quite ready, save it, you can always come back. But if you are ready? Post it before you start second-guessing. Your first edit is not supposed to be a masterpiece, it’s supposed to show you that you can do this. What comes next Once you’ve made one edit, the next ones become easier. And Edits has a lot more for you to explore as you get comfortable. Try trimming clips to tighten your pacing, experiment with filters and effects and play with captions, overlays, and keyframes. Every tool is designed to be simple at a glance and powerful when you’re ready to dig deeper. And if you ever need help along the way, the Edits Help Center has you covered. Jul 21, 2026 [[read-time]] minute read Share Copy link Listen to article Your browser does not support the audio element. Raising tweens and teens in the digital age comes with a lot of questions. That’s why YouTube is partnering with renowned clinical psychologist Dr. Becky Kennedy for an exclusive video series designed to bring practical tech guidance directly to families. With two episodes a month premiering on Good Inside’s YouTube channel , parents can expect judgement-free advice on screentime, digital literacy, healthy boundaries and more. "Parents consistently tell us they need credible, practical guidance for raising kids in the digital age," says Dr. Garth Graham, Director and Global Head of Public Health at YouTube. "Bringing her trusted, judgment-free advice to YouTube is a perfect example of our commitment to making our platform a helpful resource for families." To mark the launch, we sat down with Dr. Becky to discuss what this partnership means for families. You started your career in a traditional private clinical practice helping one family at a time, and now you reach millions across the globe. How has your definition of impact evolved over time? Dr. Becky: Honestly, my definition of impact hasn't really changed. It's always come down to the same few things for me: lives changed, people who walk away feeling more capable than they did before, and clarity where there used to be confusion. I felt all of that in private practice, one family at a time, and I never once thought of that work as small. What’s changed is the opportunity. I get to do the thing I've always cared about for more people than I ever imagined I'd reach. That's the part I am grateful for every single day. What made you decide that YouTube was the right place to build this kind of digital toolkit? Dr. Becky: This is the first time I've created a series like this, and it felt important to me that all of these conversations lived together in one place. Parents don't experience these challenges in isolation—they're all connected. And YouTube is where so many parents already go looking for answers, so it felt like the right home for this series. “YouTube is where so many parents already go looking for answers, so it felt like the right home for this series.” - Dr. Becky Kennedy, clinical psychologist and founder of Good Inside How does the launch of this new series align with your broader mission at Good Inside? Dr. Becky: Parenting in 2026 is like being asked to speak a language nobody taught us. We didn't grow up with a phone in our pocket at 15, giving us so much information and ease and comfort… and threatening to pull us away from all the in real life connection that is critical to mental health. Our kids are growing up in that world, and we are the adults in charge. This series is my attempt to share a little of that new language. You don't have to speak it perfectly to start. To be honest, no one speaks it perfectly ever. I certainly don't. But we don't stop ourselves from learning Spanish because we’ll never be fluent. We start anyway and over time it feels a bit more natural. That's the heart of Good Inside: we try to be experts in imperfect parenting. Guidance without judgment, practical, do-it-today strategies, all so parents feel a little more sturdy and a little less like they're flying blind. What was the experience like for you when bringing this series to life? Dr. Becky: Honestly? It was fun. More fun than I expected! I kind of like a hard truth, and this series kept handing me mine. It forced me to stay realistic. Every single episode, I'd catch myself asking, could I actually do this? Would it hold up in my own house? If it didn't, we kept working. How do you approach these conversations so parents feel supported rather than judged? Dr. Becky: Ugh, no. Who wants a lecture on anything? I don't. It's so pedestal-y—one person up front who's got it all figured out, everyone else taking notes on how they're falling short. I don't even love being called a parenting expert for the same reason. Available features may vary for a given election cycle. Information panels may show when you search for or watch videos related to election candidates, parties, or voting. Information panels will also feature results for specific elections sourced from non-partisan, third-party sources. Candidate information panels During an election cycle, candidate information panels may show at the top of your search results when you search for the names of eligible candidates. These panels highlight info on the candidates, such as their political party and what office they’re running for. For some elections, information panels may also surface when you search for eligible political parties. Info about candidates and parties is sourced from vetted, non-partisan, third-party sources. There’s also a link to learn more about a candidate or a political party through Google Search. Below the information panel, you may also notice: A link to the official channel of the relevant candidate or party, or An official watch card instead. Voting information panels During an election cycle, voting information panels may show at the top of your search results when you search for info on how to vote or under videos you're watching about the voting. To help you learn more about specific voting info, these panels will refer you to voting information in Google Search that’s gathered from vetted, non-partisan, third-party sources, or link you directly to those sources. Election results information panels Election results information panels may show at the top of your search results when you search for videos related to select national elections. These panels may also show under videos that discuss select national elections. The information panels may link out to non-partisan, third-party sources. Election topics information panels Information panels related to election topics may show at the top of your search results or under relevant videos. These panels link out to trustworthy information from non-partisan, third-party sources, such as a national electoral body. Learn more about topical context in information panels . FAQs Candidate information panels Where does the info for candidate information panels come from? The info is sourced from non-partisan, third-party data partners. Data partners may vary by country/region and election. Which candidates get information panels? Candidates with info sourced by a non-partisan third-party partner are eligible for an information panel. When I search for a candidate, there isn't an information panel. Why? You might need to change your search terms. Enter the exact full name of a candidate for information panels and pinned channels to surface in your search results. Keep in mind: YouTube doesn’t directly decide which candidates or parties to show a panel for. Instead we rely on vetted third-party sources for candidate and party info. If a candidate does not have a YouTube channel, they will still be featured in an information panel. If a candidate’s or party’s channel has been removed due to a YouTube policy violation, their channel may not show in search results. Candidate information panels are only available on the YouTube mobile app (Android and iOS) or on your computer.
